verdict.rationale: Netlify documents Git-push auto-deploys with per-PR preview URLs, and community users confirm the GitHub integration works. Its integration directory shows support for standard frameworks such as SvelteKit, Angular, Remix and Next.js, so existing Git and framework workflows carry over. However, nothing shows that existing CI pipelines or editors stay untouched, and deploys still route through Netlify's own CLI and config (netlify.toml). Missing for 10: documented support for existing third-party CI pipelines, editor workflow compatibility, and evidence that no Netlify-specific config or tooling is required.

support.subject: As a developer, I can keep using my existing Git, CI, editor, and framework workflows without adopting proprietary tooling

citations.quote: Auto-deploy on every push. Every PR gets a preview URL.
